subject: Evaluation roadmap and private-offer milestones (AWS) — draft MAP and pricing tranches
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechinc.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MAP + path to AWS private offer (timelines & pricing tranches)

Alex — great conversation this morning. Attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP-FinTech-v1.xlsx) that maps evaluation gates to contract milestones and the AWS private-offer steps we typically use. High level: 

- Gate 1 (POC): 2 weeks, limited tokens, standard hosted model; success metric = latency < 250ms for 95th pct, 1-2 demo integrations.
- Gate 2 (Pilot): 30 days, higher throughput, dedicated capacity for pilot; success metric = steady-state 50% of anticipated Q1 volume.
- Gate 3 (Ramp to Prod): formal commit + private offer; pricing tiers unlock with commit size and ramp schedule.

We linked each gate to an AWS private-offer staging: an evaluation Private Offer for POC (no financial commitment), then a staged-commit offer with a 3-month ramp and pricing tiers tied to monthly committed GPU-hours. See the pricing tab in the spreadsheet for tranche examples (20%, 35%, 50% discounts relative to on-demand Marketplace).

Next asks: can you confirm procurement contact and whether FinTech needs SOC2 artefacts or a DPA before we share the private-offer draft with AWS? If procurement can review the attached draft private-offer (PDF) we’ll get that into AWS as a Seller Private Offer and share the DocuSign link.

I’ll loop in Karthik on pricing engineering and Marcus for the marketplace intake.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya.n@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: MAP-FinTech-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), AWS_Private_Offer_Draft-20261118.pdf (proposal), SOW-staged-ramp.docx (SOW stub)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechinc.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@fintechinc.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + path to AWS private offer (timelines & pricing tranches)

Thanks Priya — this looks promising. A couple of clarifying items from my side / procurement: 

1) Procurement needs a baseline private-offer PDF to start the internal approval. The attached draft is fine but please confirm the billing cadence (monthly vs. upfront) and whether final discounting can change based on commit term (12 vs 24 months).
2) We will need SOC2 Type II and DPA before any production-level workload; can you attach those or point me to the compliance pack?
3) On the MAP: our security team wants the pilot to include pen-test window and a data-retention confirmation (30 days for logs).

Looping procurement for visibility; happy to schedule a quick 30m next week to align on timeline.

—Alex
Alex Johnson, Director of Platform Engineering
FinTech Inc.
alex.j@fintechinc.com

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 09:12 AM Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original MAP attached)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechinc.com>, procurement@fintechinc.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + path to AWS private offer (timelines & pricing tranches)

Alex / procurement — thanks, good flags. Quick answers inline: 

- Billing cadence: we support (A) monthly usage billing via the AWS private-offer (most common) and (B) commit-style invoices (monthly invoiced against a committed spend) for reserved-commit deals. We can model both in the private-offer; tranche discounting is applied to committed units.
- Term flexibility: discounts scale with term and commit. Example in the spreadsheet: 12-month commit = additional 5% deeper discount on top of tiered commit discounts; 24-month = additional 8%.
- Compliance pack: SOC2 Type II summary + DPA link: https://drive.example/redwood/compliance/soc2-summary.pdf (will share full artefacts with an NDA if required).
- Pilot security asks: pen-test window and 30-day retention are fine — we’ll add a pilot appendix to the SOW.

Marcus / Karthik — can you review attached private-offer draft and confirm whether we should propose a staged-commit schedule (month 1: eval credits; month 2-3: 50% commit; month 4+: full committed units) or go straight to a 90-day pilot commit? Procurement prefers staged if we can provide predictable unit pricing.

My recommended next step: 30-minute alignment with procurement + engineering next Tue 11/17 to lock the gating metrics and sign-off owners. I’ll push a calendar invite once I hear back.

Thanks,
Priya
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechinc.com>, procurement@fintechinc.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + path to AWS private offer (timelines & pricing tranches)

All — quick marketplace intake notes from our side after reviewing the PDF: 

- AWS Seller Private Offer (SPO) path: we can submit a staged-offer. For evaluation we mark the initial tranche as a non-binding evaluation grant (credits), then convert to a commitment offer that maps monthly committed units to discount tiers.
- Pricing mechanics: we prefer committing by GPU-hour equivalence (we’ll map FinTech's expected Q1 tokens to GPU-hours in the attached MAP). That gives deterministic billing on the SPO.
- Legal: we’ll need FinTech’s billing contact and signatory for the SPO; procurement@fintechinc.com is a good start.
- Timeline: if procurement signs the private-offer draft by 11/24 we can submit to AWS by 11/25 and target a Marketplace activation window of Dec 2 — Dec 9 (AWS approval varies).

Karthik — pricing question for the tiered discounts: do you want to preserve the trio of 20/35/50 or alter the middle tier to 30% for a smoother progression? Also, do we want an uplift for multi-region (us + eu) coverage?

—Marcus
Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechinc.com>, procurement@fintechinc.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + path to AWS private offer (timelines & pricing tranches)

Team / Alex — finalizing pricing suggestion and next steps. Summary for the record and for procurement: 

1) Proposed discount tranches (SPO model) — monthly committed GPU-hours mapped from forecasted tokens:
   - Tier A (eval -> pilot baseline): 15% off Marketplace list applied to first-month committed units (evaluation credits then pilot commit)
   - Tier B (pilot -> ramp): 30% off once monthly committed units >= pilot forecast; applies months 2–4 for staged-commit
   - Tier C (prod commit): 48% off for 12-month committed units (commit + ramp true-up month 4+)

2) Term uplift: +5% for 12-month agreement, +9% for 24-month. Multi-region (us + eu) +3% surcharge on list but preserves the same discount structure.

3) Operational gating: define two gating metrics to progress from pilot -> prod: sustained 95th pct latency < 300ms AND production-like throughput hitting >=50% of forecast for two consecutive weeks. If gating missed, we default to a 30-day remediation window with reduced discounts until revalidation.

4) Next actions: 
   - Procurement to confirm billing contact and preferred cadence by 11/24 (Alex/procurement).
   - Priya to upload the finalized private-offer PDF to DocuSign and AWS Seller Console by 11/25 if procurement approves.
   - Marcus to open Seller Private Offer with AWS and request expedited review.

Alex — if you agree, we’ll prepare the DocuSign SPO package today and you can sign the initial evaluation grant. After that we flip the staged-commit into an active private-offer and list the committed units.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Pricing Strategy | Redwood Inference
